evidence: Grepped site_html/*.html for "pettechlabs": found in the Organization @graph JSON-LD script on 19 pages: {"@type":"Organization",...,"logo":{"@type":"ImageObject","url":"https://www.pettechlabs.com/hubfs/Praxera/Praxera%20Logo.png"},"image":"https://www.pettechlabs.com/hubfs/Praxera/Praxera%20Logo.png",...}. The same 19 pages also carry a leftover CSS rule from the same module family: ".cell-wrapper img[src*=\"pettechlabs\"] { height:180px !important; ... }" inside a block commented "<!-- DVL-PL-CAT:START/END -->". Verified the pettechlabs.com URL itself resolves (200, image/png) via curl, confirming it is a real cross-domain reference, not a dead stub — i.e. Praxera's own structured data literally cites a DaVinci-family pet-supplement domain as the source of its logo. title: Header: "Quality & Trust" nav link visually overlaps the Praxera logo wordmark from 801px to 968px viewport width (site-wide, every page)
where: Global header module (appears on all 56 published pages) — verified on home page, https://www.praxerasupplements.com/
evidence:
Measured via work/gap.json (per-pixel sweep, 801–1600px, generated by rendering the localized home page offline per the brief's curl+file:// method): gapRight (distance from the visible right edge of the logo artwork to the left edge of "Quality & Trust") is NEGATIVE (i.e. overlapping) continuously from w=801 (–64px overlap) through w=968 (−1px), reaches 0 at w=969, and is clearly positive (74px clear) by w=1200+. Visually confirmed with shots_site/header_sweep/home_hdr_801.png and home_hdr_900.png — the text "Quality & Trust" is rendered directly on top of the "praxera" wordmark, illegible, at both widths; home_hdr_960.png still shows them touching with ~1px gap; home_hdr_970.png shows a clean, correctly-spaced header. Separately measured leftRows going from 1 to 2 (left nav wraps to two lines) somewhere between 900–952px, adding a second layout problem in roughly the same band. NOTE ON PRECISION: the offline reproduction's Google Font (Open Sans) failed to download during localization (confirmed — the cached .woff2 files for fonts.googleapis.com are actually Google's 404 HTML error page, not font binaries, so Chromium fell back to the system sans-serif font for this measurement). The qualitative defect (severe, illegible overlap across a wide desktop-nav-width band) is visually unambiguous and not in doubt, but the exact 801/968/969px crossover values could shift by roughly ±10–20px on the live site with the real Open Sans font metrics loaded. Recommend the developer confirm exact breakpoints against the live production site directly (not through this proxy-blocked-Playwright environment) before implementing a fix.
Separately checked and RULED OUT: the "Get Started" CTA button itself never collides with the logo or with "Resources" anywhere from 801–1600px — direct measurement (custom sweep script, not part of the original artifacts) shows a consistent 18–24px clear gap between the CTA and "Resources" throughout that whole range, and the CTA's left edge never overlaps the logo bounding box. The reported "Get Started button collides" concern does not reproduce; the real collision is logo-vs-"Quality & Trust" as described above.
proposed_fix: Add/adjust a CSS breakpoint for the global header so the right-nav block doesn't render inline with the logo below ~970px — either collapse to the mobile hamburger menu earlier (e.g. move the existing 800px breakpoint up to ~970px) or reduce the nav's horizontal padding/font-size in that band so "Quality & Trust" clears the logo. Re-verify the exact px thresholds on the live site (real fonts) before finalizing the CSS change.

title: /get-started causes ~350px of horizontal scroll on mobile (390px viewport) due to a hardcoded inline width
evidence: work/measure.json at width=390 for slug get-started: hscroll=350, overflowCount=14, document.documentElement.scrollWidth=740 vs clientWidth=390. Traced to the exact cause in the page's rich-text module source (work/render/get-started/page.html, and live site_html copy): a hand-authored inline style `<div style="width: 45em; color: #231f20; background-color: #ffffff;">` wraps the "Build Your product line from over 190 supplements" checklist block. 45em = 720px at the default 16px root font size, a fixed width that does not shrink for mobile, so the whole block (and everything after it in that column) is forced to 720px+20px offset regardless of viewport, producing the 350px of horizontal scroll measured at 390px width. Re-verified independently with a fresh Playwright pass against the offline render (not reusing the artifact's numbers blindly): confirms scrollWidth 740 / clientWidth 390, and identifies the 7 overflowing checklist rows plus their container div as the offenders, all left=20 right=740 width=720.
proposed_fix: In the Get Started page's rich-text module content, remove the inline `style="width: 45em; ..."` on that div (or change it to `max-width: 45em; width: 100%;`) so it scales down on narrow viewports. This is a single edit inside one rich-text field.

evidence: Exhaustively checked: (1) work/image_status.json (148 sampled image URLs) — all 200. (2) work/assets2_status.json (332 broader asset URLs incl. srcset width variants) — all 200. (3) Independently re-crawled every , srcset entry, and CSS url(...) reference across all 56 cached published-page HTML files (389 distinct URLs total) and curl-checked every one — all 200, none zero-byte. (4) Searched all cached HTML/other artifacts for the word "infographic" as a filename or link — it appears only as a plain word inside one sentence on /how-to-sell-supplements ("Create blog posts, videos, and infographics..."), not as a link to any PDF or asset, and no PDF or asset in the crawled data has "infographic" in its name. All PDFs referenced from the site (Definitive Guide, Ingredients Guide, 15 product Sell Sheets on /top-sellers) return 200. Separately, the screenshot pipeline appeared to show several blank/missing product or category images (aging.html's 7-tile category grid, detox.html's guide thumbnail, top-sellers.html's "ADK" bottle) — investigated these directly with a fresh Playwright pass: all of the underlying image files load fine (HTTP 200, valid image data) and render correctly once the page is scrolled so the image enters the viewport (naturalWidth confirmed non-zero after scroll+decode) — these are native `loading="lazy"` images that simply had not been triggered yet when the prior QA pass's full-page screenshot was taken, not actually-broken images. Given all of this, the specific "2 broken images"/"missing infographic PDF" the owner has in mind were not found by any method available in this pass.
proposed_fix: Ask the owner for the exact page URL(s) and, if possible, the specific image filename(s)/PDF they're thinking of — recommend checking whether they're on a blog post (out of this WEBSITE-scope crawl) rather than one of the 56 site pages, or whether the asset has since been fixed.
